**Test image observations:**
- Tomato leaf, mostly green with prominent yellowing/orange necrosis at the left tip/margin
- Dark brown-black necrotic tissue at the leaf tip
- Multiple small dark spots scattered across the green portions of the leaf
- No visible webbing, no white powdery coating, no mosaic/mottling pattern

**Key visual features:**
- Small dark spots with apparent dark borders on the leaf lamina → characteristic of Septoria Leaf Spot
- Marginal necrosis with yellowing at the tip — Septoria commonly starts on lower leaves and can cause extensive yellow-to-necrotic patches as spots coalesce
- No concentric rings or large target-like lesions (rules out Early Blight / Target Spot)
- No V-shaped lesion clearly defined from margin (less consistent with Verticillium Wilt)

**Target_Spot reference comparison:** The reference shows dark green leaves with small inconspicuous spots — the test image pattern with the marginal necrosis and scattered small dark lesions aligns better with Septoria Leaf Spot's description (multiple small spots coalescing, causing extensive leaf destruction).

{"prediction": "Septoria_Leaf_Spot", "confidence": 0.62, "reasoning": "The leaf shows multiple small dark-bordered spots scattered across the lamina consistent with Septoria Leaf Spot lesions (<1/8 inch, dark perimeter). The prominent yellowing and necrosis at the leaf tip is consistent with coalescence of Septoria lesions causing extensive tissue destruction. No concentric rings (Early Blight), no webbing (Spider Mites), no powdery coating (Powdery Mildew), and no clear V-shaped margin lesion (Verticillium Wilt) are visible."}
